title: Add X-Usenet-IPFS-Root-CID header for multi-block DAG articles
description:
Why: large articles (or future binary articles) may be stored as multi-block IPLD DAGs with a root CID that links to content blocks. X-Usenet-IPFS-CID gives the content CID; X-Usenet-IPFS-Root-CID gives the DAG root that links everything. For single-block articles (all v1 text articles), these two values are identical and Root-CID is omitted to avoid noise.

What: if the stored article has a separate root CID distinct from the content CID (i.e. it is a multi-block DAG), inject X-Usenet-IPFS-Root-CID: <root-cidv1> into ARTICLE and HEAD responses. For single-block articles, omit the header. This allows Corundum and IPLD traversal tools to start from the root and walk the DAG rather than assuming a flat single-block structure.
design: Requires schema support in the article storage model for a root_cid field separate from content_cid. In v1, all articles are single-block so this header is never emitted; the field and injection logic are implemented but always produce no output. This future-proofs the reader for v2 binary support without protocol changes.
